newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-PIENAAR AXING CALLED "DESPERATELY SAD".
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-PIENAAR AXING CALLED "DESPERATELY SAD".

text.p: Former South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) chief executive Edward Griffiths said on Monday the omission of Francois Pienaar from the Springbok tour party was "desperately sad".
"I worked very closely with Francois Pienaar in 1994 and 1995 and I find it desperately sad that he should have been treated in this way," Griffiths told Reuters.

"When I heard he had been axed, I was more shocked than when I received my own fax (of dismissal from SARFU by Louis Luyt). If you could see Francois in team meetings and preparations, he is such a professional man who gave his all to Springbok rugby. He deserved a lot better.

"The contrast between 1995 and now could hardly be more stark. What we did then involved basic decency and doing things in the correct way. But nothing we did was complicated and I don't want to claim any kind of heroism because most of it was common sense."

Pienaar's omission from the 36-man squad named by coach Andre Markgraaff on Saturday completes the entire dismantling of the Springbok managament team which steered South Africa to victory in the 1995 rugby World Cup.

Coach Kitch Christie left his position on the grounds of ill-health, manager Morne du Plessis bowed out after the three-test series against New Zealand in August and Griffiths was summarily dismissed from office by SARFU president Louis Luyt via a facimile message.

Griffiths has since taken over as general manager of South African Television's (SATV's) Topsport service and, in that capacity, he was astounded by SARFU's bungled treatment of the televised announcement of the South African tour party on Saturday.

M-Net, the South African subscriber television network, was scheduled to announce the 36-man squad live at 5.50 p.m. on Saturday. However, the team was only released to M-Net half an hour later while Markgraaff only made himself available to the media a full hour after the scheduled time.

"If I was a TV company who had committed millions of rand for the rights of rugby - a sum which constitutes about 70 percent of SARFU's total income - I would have expected better treatment," Griffiths said.
